ctx.x: Now, I know when I left Benny Goodman's band, I left it in 1943 and I went into the studios. I had a good friend, Gil Evans, who used to needle me all of the time about it. And he'd see me up the Union, collecting my checks, and he'd make corny remarks, "$1 million, $2 million," or something. And I always felt a little apologetic about it. But I had a family to support and I have children, and I didn't believe that I had the right to go out on the road and enjoy myself playing in jazz bands or whatever and leave…

And truthfully, I enjoyed studio work. But what sort of took the stigma off from it was within the first five years, I mention names, I guess it won't hurt; I went to hear Lee Konitz one night. At that time he was a big jazz player and everything. And he was talking to me and he said, you know,
man, just because I'm a jazz player, you know, I can read and spell. If there are any gigs you'd like to do, I'd appreciate it if you'd fix me up.
